title: Security posture discovery with Orchid Solutions
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs
summary: Orchid is evaluating Redwood for a mix of hosted and private deployments for customer-facing features that touch regulated data. Primary blockers are SOC2 Type II evidence, SSO integration with Okta, fine-grained RBAC, audit log retention guarantees, and BYOK for encryption. Redwood AE/SE will share security docs, SOC2 report, and propose a dedicated POC with a checklist for infra to validate - includes a performance benchmark and KMS integration trial.
action_items: Maya Singh: Share Redwood security whitepaper, SOC2 Type II report, ISO cert refs (due 2026-04-20)
Ethan Park: Schedule technical deep dive with Samir and infra team to discuss VPC/private deployment options and KMS integration (due 2026-04-23)
Claire Rodriguez: Send example data retention / compliance policy and list of regs that will apply (due 2026-04-22)
Lena Wu: Provide Okta SAML metadata and SSO requirements (due 2026-04-21)
next_steps: Redwood to email security package + SOC2 report
Schedule SE-led deep-dive on dedicated/private deployment and KMS
Agree on scope for 2-week dedicated POC including throughput and encryption test
Customer to share timeline and compliance checklist
transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-04-18
- Time: 16:00 PT
- Duration: ~42 minutes
- Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Claire (CTO, Orchid), Samir (Head Infra), Lena (Security)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be imperfect):
Orchid wants to understand Redwood's security posture across Hosted, Dedicated and Private deployments. They asked about SOC2/ISO, SSO and SAML, RBAC controls, audit logs/retention, KMS/BYOK, encryption at-rest/in-transit and data purging policies. Redwood AE/SE outlined typical architecture differences and promised security docs + a POC checklist.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I think we've got a handful of agenda items, mostly around security posture and which deployment model makes sense for Orchid. Quick intros?
[00:07] Claire: Hi, Claire here, CTO at Orchid. We run a B2B analytics platform, some PHI-like datasets, not full PHI yet, but definitely PII and finance records. I'm primarily here to understand compliance fit.
[00:15] Samir: Samir, infra. We'll own any network/VPC work. Interested in the dedicated/private options and how they integrate into our KMS and audit pipeline.
[00:22] Lena: Lena, security lead. SOC2/ISO are table stakes. Want to know about SSO, RBAC, logs and retention, and who holds the keys.
[00:30] Maya: Great, thanks. Ethan and I from Redwood — Ethan focuses on infra and SE stuff — we'll run through our posture and answer detail questions. Just to set expectations: we support Hosted API, Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU capacity), and Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem style). Each has different controls for keys and network.
[00:45] Ethan: Quick add — hosted is fastest to go live; Dedicated gives isolation and reserved capacity; Private is where you bring the control plane into your VPC or on-prem and we support BYOK patterns there. There can be some mis-speech in docs sometimes, sorry, yes BYOK — bring your own key.
[01:05] Claire: High-level question — are you SOC2 Type II and ISO certified? We need to know the latest report and which parts of the stack are covered.
[01:12] Maya: Yes, Redwood has SOC2 Type II. We maintain ISO 27001 as well. We'll share the attestation and the SOC2 report — note that for hosted we hold the infrastructure, so our SOC2 covers those operations; for Dedicated we have an overlay and can provide architecture scoping for the work; for Private deployments, customers often have their own audit scope. We'll send the most recent reports after the call.
[01:35] Lena: Okay, we need to check scope — is logging and key management included in the SOC2? Specifically audit trails for access to customer data and key usage.
[01:44] Ethan: Good question. Our SOC2 covers operational controls for the hosted service including access control and logging. For KMS usage, hosted supports CMKs — customer-managed keys via cloud KMS integrations for Dedicated and Private we can do BYOK where your KMS/HSM stays in your account or network. The SOC2 will show our controls around key handling but for BYOK the key lifecycle is in your domain, so that falls under customer controls.
[02:10] Samir: So with Dedicated we can still use our own KMS or do we have to use Redwood's key store?
[02:16] Ethan: For Dedicated, we support a mode where keys are customer-held in your cloud project — you can configure our runtime to use a customer CMK for at-rest encryption. There's some work to wire up IAM and grant least privilege to the nodes for decrypt operations. For Private/on-prem, keys never leave your environment if you prefer HSM.
[02:34] Lena: What's the retention window for audit logs? We have a 7-year retention requirement for some records.
[02:41] Maya: Default retention for the hosted console logs is 90 days, but we have add-ons for extended retention. For Dedicated and Private, retention is configurable and you can ship logs into your own SIEM or long term storage. We'll include details on log exports and RBAC for log access.
[03:00] Claire: On SSO — we use Okta and Azure AD. We need SAML-based SSO, SCIM for provisioning ideally, and ability to map groups to roles.
[03:09] Ethan: We support SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning on the enterprise plan. RBAC maps to groups; you can configure role bindings so engineers, admins, and ops teams get least privilege. For Redwood Private, it's often integrated directly with your IdP via the VPC connector.
[03:30] Lena: Any precedent for deep integration with our IdP, like certificate rotation cadence or metadata polling?
[03:36] Ethan: We can support metadata refresh and have runbooks for cert rotation. For automated SCIM provisioning we honor group sync schedules from Okta, and you can configure role mapping policies via the Console or API.
[03:52] Samir: We have strict network egress requirements. For Hosted, does traffic ever route through other regions or vendors? Data residency is a hard requirement — some customers must keep tokens in eu-west only.
[04:02] Maya: Hosted is region-aware; we have EU and US regions and can restrict processing to a region. For stricter requirements or no egress, Dedicated or Private is the recommended path — Private puts the runtime in your VPC so nothing goes outside your network unless you configure it.
[04:22] Claire: For the POC we want to validate latency and cost for embeddings and generation — and also test that persistence doesn't leak PII. How do you handle request-level data retention and purge?
[04:33] Ethan: By default, request logs and payloads are retained per retention policy; we have a redaction feature and can disable request logging. For customers with stringent needs we offer no-persistence mode where we don't write payloads, and for Private deployments you can choose to never persist. We'll note that some telemetry for billing and metrics is still generated but can be aggregated.
[04:58] Lena: What about model caching, prefix caches, KV caches — do those store raw customer text? If so, where are those stored and how are they encrypted?
[05:06] Ethan: The KV cache is ephemeral per node; for hosted, it's encrypted at-rest with service keys, and for Dedicated/Private you can put the cache on volumes encrypted with your customer key. We'll share architecture docs that show cache boundaries.
[05:23] Claire: Any customers in our vertical who have done Private deployments?
[05:28] Maya: Yes, a couple of fintech and health customers — we'll anonymize references but can share case notes.
[05:34] Samir: On the network side, what's the setup time for a Private deployment? We have a two-week window for a pilot if it's feasible.
[05:42] Ethan: For a Private VPC connector, typical onboarding is 2-4 weeks depending on IP allowlists, firewall rules, and IAM. For fully on-prem, it's longer. For Dedicated in your cloud account it's often 1-2 weeks if infra is ready. We'll scope the POC to a 2-week run with a pre-checklist.
[06:00] Lena: Can you support bring-your-own-HSM? We run an HSM for key material.
[06:06] Ethan: Yes, for Private we have integrations that let you keep keys in your HSM and we call via a secure connector; for Dedicated we can integrate cloud KMS or customer-managed keys. We'll confirm supported HSM vendors in the doc pack.
[06:22] Claire: About RBAC: do you have IAM style policies or only a few pre-built roles? We want fine grain controls — e.g., who can deploy a model, who can change rollout policies, who can access logs — these need to be mapped to our internal groups.
[06:36] Maya: We have role templates out of the box and support custom roles with permissions. For larger accounts we also support role inheritance and audit hooks so you can forward audit events to SIEM.
[06:48] Lena: Audit logs — do they capture token-level events, model changes, admin actions, API calls?
[06:54] Ethan: Yes, audit logs capture control plane events (user actions, model updates, rollouts), API policy events, and token usage. For Hosted we retain per policy; for Dedicated/Private you can stream logs to your SIEM. We also support signed log delivery.
[07:12] Samir: If we run a POC that includes throughput tests, what's the best way to test per-token latency without skewing results with multi-tenant noisy neighbors?
[07:21] Ethan: For Dedicated/Private you get isolated capacity so you avoid noisy neighbors; for hosted we provide performance profiles and we can run a benchmarking job on a reserved capacity instance for a short time. We'll propose a dedicated benchmark node for the POC.
[07:36] Claire: Any compliance certifications for crypto modules or HSM? FIPS?
[07:41] Maya: Our cloud KMS integrations can use FIPS-compliant providers in certain regions; for HSM we work with FIPS validated modules through the customer HSM. We'll check specifics and include them in the security pack.
[07:55] Lena: Are there any known gaps or controls we should be aware of? We need a risk register so we can sign off internally.
[08:02] Ethan: We can produce a responsibility matrix (shared responsibility) that lists what Redwood controls and what the customer is responsible for. For example, Redwood controls the hosted runtime ops, patching, and infra; the customer controls IAM in their cloud for Dedicated and Private, and data classification decisions. There are typical gaps around long-term archival of raw request payloads — we can offer options but need to agree on the configuration.
[08:30] Maya: Quick recap of asks: Lena wants SOC2 scope details and audit retention info; Samir wants KMS/HSM integration details and onboarding timeline; Claire wants POC scope for latency/cost tests. We'll follow up with docs and propose the POC checklist.
[08:45] Claire: Sounds good. One last question — are there per-route encryption or token scoping capabilities so that different teams can have separate keys?
[08:53] Ethan: We support per-tenant keys in Dedicated and Private setups; you can scope keys per project/route. For hosted it's more limited but we do have token scoping and some key scoping via separate tenants. We'll clarify limitations in the doc pack.
[09:10] Lena: Great, please include sample artifact — e.g., an example audit log event schema so we can validate ingestion.
[09:17] Maya: Will do. We'll email security pack with SOC2/ISO certificates, the responsibility matrix, an audit event schema, and a POC checklist by Tuesday.
[09:26] Claire: Thanks everyone; we'll review and come back with a proposed timeline.
[09:30] Maya: Thanks all, we'll follow up with the items.

Call end.
